pr_title: feat(citations): add the DOI registry resolver the citation gate never had (#422
title: Preserve unpublished status for posted-content subtypes
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve unpublished status for posted-content subtypes**

For a registry record with `type: "posted-content"` and `subtype: "working_paper"`, `"report"`, or `"other"`, preferring `subtype` discards the posted-content classification and assigns `version: "published"`. Crossref explicitly describes [posted content as not formally published](https://support.crossref.org/hc/en-us/articles/213126346-Posted-content-includes-preprints). With an injected working-paper record, `verify_citation` consequently returns `supported` for a citation incorrectly claiming `version: "published"`. Check the parent type before assigning published status, and omit the version when the registry does not establish a supported classification.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/citation_resolver.py:137-143 merges the two fields: `subtype = str(message.get("subtype") or message.get("type") or "").lower()`, then tests that merged value against `("posted-content", "preprint")` and otherwise assigns `version = "published"`. A record with `type: "posted-content"` and `subtype: "working_paper"` therefore never matches the parent type and is stamped published.

pr_title: #344: bind resumed context to the current request and its freshness
title: Invalidate provider receipts when restarting with new context
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invalidate provider receipts when restarting with new context**

When an answer completes but its Jev review is interrupted, resuming with a changed instruction now rebuilds context and clears the checkpoint answer, but retains the lifecycle's completed provider receipts. Restarting at round 1 then uses the same `request_id:chat-answer:1` key, so `LifecycleCoordinator.provider_call()` returns the old answer without invoking the answer provider. I reproduced this through `run_prompt()` with an apples request followed by `continue with instead explain oranges`: context was gathered twice, but the answer provider ran only once and the original answer was returned. Namespace answer/review receipts by the new context/request generation when invalidating reuse, while preserving accounting history.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/hourglass_lifecycle.py:1259-1262 keys the answer receipt as `lifecycle_state["request_id"] + f":chat-answer:{round_no}"`, and harness/lifecycle.py:403-410 returns the cached `result` for any completed call id before invoking. The resumed lifecycle keeps its original `request_id` (harness/lifecycle.py:140-151 adopts the same state), and nothing in hourglass_lifecycle.py clears `usage.provider_calls`, so a changed instruction that rebuilds context still replays the round-1 answer.

pr_title: feat(citations): audit a declared bibliography at the report face (#422)
title: Require citation assessments to cover the report's actual claims
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require citation assessments to cover the report's actual claims**

When `claims` contains entries omitted from `citation_claims`, this wrapper audits only the latter and still lets `lint-claims` label the entire report `citation_verified: true`. Using the new test fixture, adding an unsupported `c2` to `claims` while leaving `citation_claims` unchanged produces exit 0, an empty unresolved list, and a verified label despite never assessing `c2`. Validate that the citation assessments cover the report's actual claim IDs, and leave missing assessments unresolved before granting the report-level label.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/citation_resolver.py:196-199 passes only `report.get("citation_claims")` into `audit_citations`, which labels the report from exactly the claims it was given (harness/citation_verify.py:417-421), and harness/cli.py:486-492 publishes that label as `citation_verified`. Nothing compares `citation_claims` against the report's `claims`, so a claim omitted from the audited list is never assessed and the report-level label still passes.

pr_title: feat(web): shared result reviewer with typed relevance bands (#660)
title: Preserve billed spend and unknown liability on cancellation
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve billed spend and unknown liability on cancellation**

If the reviewer raises `ProviderUsageUnknown` or a post-dispatch `ToolCancelled`, `_release()` reconciles its reservation at zero, losing any `known_cost` and releasing money that may already have been billed. Reproducing either exception leaves the governor with zero spent, outstanding, and unknown liability, allowing subsequent calls to reuse that budget. Use `_settle_cancelled(reservation, exc)`, as the other evaluation methods do, to book known charges and retain unknown liability.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/jev_policy.py:2022-2024 catches `(ToolCancelled, ProviderUsageUnknown)` in `evaluate_result_relevance` with `self._release(reservation)`, and `_release` is documented at :665-667 as settling the reservation at zero. `_settle_cancelled` exists and is used by `_release_reservation` at :582-591, but not on this path, so a known charge is dropped and unknown liability is not retained.

pr_title: feat(web): shared result reviewer with typed relevance bands (#660)
title: Fail closed when reviewer initialization fails
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail closed when reviewer initialization fails**

When reviewer construction fails in `_handle_conversation`, its exception handler leaves `web_policy=None` and still calls the gatherer. This branch then admits every unpinned result without a verdict or an evidence-block outage disclosure. That is a reviewer setup outage, not the supported no-key case, which already has an explicit local verdict path in `evaluate_result_relevance`. Route an absent reviewer through the withholding/outage behavior rather than returning the original evidence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/web.py:798-802 handles an absent reviewer by emitting `web_result_review_unavailable` and returning `ordered` unchanged: no verdict, no withholding, and no `reviewer` evidence-block entry (that entry is only appended on the `outage` branch at :838-845). harness/conversation_lifecycle.py:155-160 leaves `web_policy = None` when reviewer construction raises, so the outage path reaches this admission branch.

pr_title: feat(web): shared result reviewer with typed relevance bands (#660)
title: Carry reviewer costs back to the request lifecycle
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Carry reviewer costs back to the request lifecycle**

For a billed relevance review, the policy settles the charge in the governor, but this function discards both the evaluation result and `structural['cost']`, returning only sources. Consequently, neither conversation result costs nor the hourglass `total_cost` and checkpoint `known_cost` include this new provider call. Besides underreporting spend, an hourglass continuation reconstructs its governor from that incomplete checkpoint and regains budget already spent on retrieval review. Return and accumulate the review receipt alongside the sources, including billed outage responses.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/web.py:798-801 keeps only `structural.get("results")` (read at :812); `structural['cost']` is never returned, and the function's only result is the filtered source list. Its caller, harness/conversation_lifecycle.py:588-589, returns that list alone, so a billed relevance review never reaches conversation result cost or the hourglass `total_cost`/checkpoint `known_cost`.

pr_title: fix(hourglass): bind a saved route decision to the request it judged (#344)
title: Bind the provider-call cache key to the rerouted request
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the provider-call cache key to the rerouted request**

When a real interrupted lifecycle contains a completed `:chat-route-review` provider receipt, rejecting `route_preflight` here still does not trigger a fresh review: the subsequent `self.lifecycle.provider_call` uses the unchanged request ID and call key, and `LifecycleCoordinator.provider_call` returns that receipt's cached result without invoking `evaluate_route_once`. I reproduced a changed bicycle-explanation request retaining the old native web-research route with zero fresh route evaluations; this change then records the new prompt in `route_request_prompt`, incorrectly certifying the stale decision as belonging to it. Use a request-bound provider-call key when rerouting, and cover a persisted lifecycle containing the completed route receipt rather than only the synthetic payload used by the new tests.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/hourglass_lifecycle.py:939-945 calls `provider_call` with the key `lifecycle_state["request_id"] + ":chat-route-review"`, and harness/lifecycle.py:403-410 returns the cached completed result for that id before invoking. The reuse predicate at :572-606 does reject a changed request, but rejecting it does not change the call id, so a persisted lifecycle that already holds a completed route receipt returns the old decision; `route_request_prompt` is then overwritten at :969 with the new prompt.

pr_title: feat(research): shared request-bound ResearchPlan and native review (#342)
title: Preserve the judgment's original plan and request binding
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the judgment's original plan and request binding**

When a native judgment for one plan is passed alongside a revised plan, this helper replaces the judgment's `plan_hash`, `request_hash`, and `revision` with those of the supplied plan. Consequently, an acceptance for query A can authorize an entirely different query B: `validate_plan` accepts the newly stamped receipt and `execute_plan` sends B without native review. Preserve and verify the binding fields from the judgment rather than assigning a new binding during receipt construction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/research_plan.py:521-526 builds the `PlanApproval` from the supplied plan (`plan.hash()`, `plan.request_hash`, `plan.revision`) and never reads the binding fields the judgment carries; harness/jev_policy.py:2128-2130 and :2162-2165 do emit `plan_hash`, `request_hash` and `revision` in the structural envelope. A judgment made for one plan can therefore be restamped onto another, and `validate_plan` (:405-444) then accepts the new binding.

pr_title: feat(research): shared request-bound ResearchPlan and native review (#342)
title: Bind the fetch policy before passing the default fetcher
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the fetch policy before passing the default fetcher**

For an accepted URL plan using the default transport, `execute_plan` eventually invokes `_fetch_source`, which calls `fetch_fn(url)`, but `fetch_url` requires an `allowed_hosts` argument. This path therefore raises an uncaught `TypeError` before fetching anything. Unlike the legacy path, it also never forwards `allow_any_public` or `named_hosts`. Pass an adapter that supplies the configured fetch policy; the existing one-argument test doubles conceal this failure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/web.py:867-875 hands `fetch_url` (or the injected `fetch_url_fn`) straight to `execute_plan` as the plan's `fetch_fn`, while `fetch_url` at :616-617 requires `allowed_hosts` and the legacy branch at :900-905 passes it explicitly. harness/research_plan.py:798-803 then calls `fetch_fn(url)` with one positional argument, and `_fetch_source` catches only `HarnessError`, so the `TypeError` escapes an accepted URL plan and the gatherer returns nothing.

pr_title: feat(research): shared request-bound ResearchPlan and native review (#342)
title: Enforce the accepted plan's aggregate source limit
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the accepted plan's aggregate source limit**

For a multi-query plan, each search appends up to `max_results` sources and every fetch appends another source, but execution never reads `plan.max_sources`. For example, a valid accepted plan with two searches, `max_results=3`, and `max_sources=1` returns six sources. This exceeds the source budget included in the reviewed plan and exposes downstream consumers to evidence beyond that bound. Enforce the aggregate source limit across search and fetch results.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/research_plan.py:771-781 appends every search's `max_results` sources and one source per fetch, and never reads `plan.max_sources`; the field is validated at :354-355 as a plan property only. A two-query plan with `max_results=3` and `max_sources=1` therefore returns six sources, past the budget the reviewed plan carried.

pr_title: fix(hourglass): bind a saved route decision to the accepted plan (#344)
title: Invalidate the provider receipt when the plan changes
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invalidate the provider receipt when the plan changes**

When resuming a real lifecycle that already completed its route review, rejecting the checkpoint here does not actually obtain a new decision: the subsequent `provider_call` still uses the unchanged `<request_id>:chat-route-review` key, and `LifecycleCoordinator.provider_call` returns its cached completed result (`harness/lifecycle.py:403–410`). Running once with plan A and then resuming with plan B leaves `evaluate_request_workflow` at one invocation while saving the old route under B's hash. Bind the provider-call identity to the plan as well, or otherwise invalidate that receipt when the binding fails; the new adapter test misses this because its synthetic checkpoint has no completed provider-call receipt.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/hourglass_lifecycle.py:939-945 keys the route review as `lifecycle_state["request_id"] + ":chat-route-review"`, which carries no plan binding, and harness/lifecycle.py:403-410 returns the completed receipt. `_saved_route_plan_reusable` at :610-660 rejects a changed plan, but the rejection only stops reuse; the subsequent `provider_call` still replays the cached decision, which :969 then records under the new plan's hash.

pr_title: fix(hourglass): bind a saved route decision to the accepted plan (#344)
title: Preserve the saved approval when resuming without a new one
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the saved approval when resuming without a new one**

When a caller resumes with the same `research_plan` and omits the optional `plan_approval`, the reuse predicate correctly accepts the saved native receipt, but this assignment then replaces it with empty fields and `native=False`. The next continuation consequently rejects the unchanged plan with `plan-receipt-not-native`, losing the approval evidence that justified reuse. Preserve the existing receipt when reusing the same plan without a replacement approval instead of serializing `None` over it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/hourglass_lifecycle.py:1061-1066 writes `checkpoint["plan_approval"]` from `plan_approval` alone, falling back to `{"decision": "", "native": False, ...}` when the caller supplied none. A resume that re-supplies the identical plan without a replacement approval leaves `plan_approval` as `None` whenever `saved_plan_approval` declines to rebuild it, so the recorded receipt is replaced by the empty non-native dict and the next continuation fails `plan-receipt-not-native` at :638-642.
